scope: Behavior-level provenance for the 2026 agent capability absorption work. This does not replace the historical limitations documented in docs/ip-provenance.md.

records.behaviorContract: Route every own-agent ingress through one RunLoopWithOptions kernel, limit RunMode to phase directives, and reduce every typed terminal without transport-specific success drift.
nonCopiedConstraints: The RunMode contract, terminal envelope, and ingress reducers are independently designed for Corelay Code's existing kernel.
No external agent loop, orchestration controller, or terminal reducer implementation is copied.

records.behaviorContract: Resolve one immutable run profile before execution and expose only copied, validated policy values.
nonCopiedConstraints: No upstream source file is vendored or embedded.
The profile is an independent Go value object fitted to Corelay Code's existing RunLoopWithOptions composition.

records.behaviorContract: Select native-only, bounded text recovery, or multi-format response processing without leaking fallback reasoning into history.
nonCopiedConstraints: Parser control flow and typed outcomes were designed for Corelay Code's canonical SSE blocks.
Fixtures are newly authored minimal examples rather than copied upstream test bodies.

records.behaviorContract: Prefer declared native structured calls and validate them against the active immutable catalog before any textual recovery.
nonCopiedConstraints: Corelay Code keeps its existing canonical ToolUseBlock representation.
No upstream identifiers or implementation functions are reused.

records.behaviorContract: Decode bounded Hermes tool_call wrappers, reject ambiguity and duplicate keys, then apply catalog/schema validation.
nonCopiedConstraints: The decoder is an independent Go implementation.
Corpus strings contain only minimal protocol syntax needed for interoperability.

records.behaviorContract: Decode the documented Liquid marker and safe literal subset with hard depth, size, and call-count limits.
nonCopiedConstraints: The literal parser was written independently in Go.
No JavaScript parser code or upstream fixtures are copied or translated line by line.

records.behaviorContract: Recover complete fenced or whole-response bare JSON and bounded suffix-only truncation without inventing middle tokens.
nonCopiedConstraints: Corelay Code uses strict duplicate-key and ambiguity rejection not imported from upstream.
Tests use newly authored payloads and deterministic fuzz seeds.

records.behaviorContract: Render a validated compact or strict plan anchor on every configured iteration without creating a second planner loop.
nonCopiedConstraints: The anchor schema and renderer are Corelay Code-specific.
Only the general behavior goal was retained.

records.behaviorContract: Bind strict Definition of Done criteria to one run-owned revision-CAS completion contract, accept only indexed execution evidence, withhold unapproved completion prose, and persist one typed terminal across receipt, stream, recorder, and durable session.
nonCopiedConstraints: The criterion IDs, evidence index, ReportCompletion identity proof, correction policy, and terminal metadata schema are Corelay Code-specific.
No external completion implementation or prompt text is copied.

records.behaviorContract: Require a fresh workspace-scoped read revision before editing an existing file and preserve the ledger through common dispatch.
nonCopiedConstraints: The digest ledger and stale-read decisions are Corelay Code-specific.
No external edit implementation is included.

records.behaviorContract: Fingerprint normalized tool name, arguments, target revision, failure class, and plan step to bound exact repeated actions, then publish one content-free audit through summary, receipt, and terminal output.
nonCopiedConstraints: The SHA-256 fingerprint fields are Corelay Code-specific.
No upstream repetition implementation is copied.

records.behaviorContract: Resolve iteration, consecutive-error-round, and repeated-action ceilings from the immutable run profile and enforce each limit in the existing agent loop and common dispatcher.
nonCopiedConstraints: Corelay Code keeps separate iteration, error-round, and canonical action-fingerprint limits.
No external stop-loop implementation is copied.

records.behaviorContract: Authorize every serial and parallel call through one schema, path, permission, approval, provenance, and pre-hook boundary before scheduling.
nonCopiedConstraints: The dispatcher extends Corelay Code's existing executor contract.
No external scheduler or permission source is embedded.

records.behaviorContract: Open one redacted, session-bound approval request, await allow-once or deny, and fail closed on absence, timeout, disconnect, or duplicate resolution.
nonCopiedConstraints: The in-memory broker and HTTP/CLI/Web composition are Corelay Code-specific.
Raw tool input is intentionally excluded from broker records.

records.behaviorContract: Select only a probed OS isolation adapter satisfying the requested capabilities and never downgrade Preferred or Required to host execution.
nonCopiedConstraints: Adapters are independently implemented for Corelay Code's sandbox.Runner contract.
Open Interpreter or Codex sandbox source is not vendored, translated, or linked.

records.behaviorContract: Persist versioned transcripts with canonical workspace ownership, atomic revision compare-and-swap, lifecycle metadata, and the same typed errors across HTTP, Web, and advertised ACP session operations.
nonCopiedConstraints: The JSON schema and filesystem layout are Corelay Code-specific.
No upstream session storage source or fixture is copied.

records.behaviorContract: Persist a content-free execution marker after authorization and identity binding but before every tool start event and executor call; require explicit reconciliation after failure or hard exit, and atomically clear the exact marker only with a successful transcript and terminal commit.
nonCopiedConstraints: The interruption digest, aggregate marker, side-effect enum, and CAS lifecycle are Corelay Code-specific.
Raw tool inputs and storage paths are excluded from durable markers and client errors.

records.behaviorContract: Fork one immutable parent revision through the advertised HTTP and Web mutation surface into an isolated child with copied history and preserved lineage, while ACP truthfully omits an undefined fork method and preserves child lineage on resume.
nonCopiedConstraints: Fork allocation, lineage validation, and workspace rules are Corelay Code-specific.
No upstream session implementation is reused.

records.behaviorContract: Use opaque crypto IDs, canonical digest directories, containment checks, collision detection, and fsync-plus-rename persistence.
nonCopiedConstraints: The storage key and migration algorithm are independently designed for Corelay Code.
No external session path implementation is included.

records.behaviorContract: Persist successful large tool results before any model-visible or durable boundary, expose only canonical redacted bounded references and paging, and fail closed without raw fallback when durable publication fails.
nonCopiedConstraints: The content-addressed namespace, committed-reference inventory, and checked-store disposition are independently designed for Corelay Code.
No external blob store, session format, or large-result fixture is copied or embedded.

records.behaviorContract: Expose a bounded stable ACP v1 newline JSON-RPC transport, typed durable session and prompt routing, cancellation isolation, redacted permission requests, session-owned stdio MCP, and the same hard-exit durable execution journal as HTTP without advertising unsupported optional methods or transports.
nonCopiedConstraints: Wire contracts were independently modeled from the pinned public JSON schema; no upstream implementation source or generated bindings are vendored or translated.
The bridge delegates execution to Corelay Code's existing RunLoopWithOptions kernel and independently owns only ACP translation, session state, and stdio MCP lifetime.

records.behaviorContract: Separate evidence-policy disposition from completion confidence and persist exactly one verified, partially-verified, unverified, or blocked terminal state through the sanitized receipt boundary.
nonCopiedConstraints: The state table and mixed-evidence precedence are independently defined for Corelay Code.
No upstream completion or receipt schema is copied.

records.behaviorContract: Deep-clone and redact receipt values before serialization while preserving only bounded evidence metadata.
nonCopiedConstraints: The redaction corpus and serializer boundary are Corelay Code-specific.
No external receipt format is copied.

records.behaviorContract: Record command and artifact SHA-256 digests, relative paths, typed status, and atomic receipt location without raw command disclosure.
nonCopiedConstraints: The wire payload and digest fields are Corelay Code-specific.
No upstream evidence schema is embedded.

records.behaviorContract: Compose a bounded resolved prompt suffix and optional plan anchor into the canonical system request exactly once per run policy.
nonCopiedConstraints: The prompt composition is expressed through Corelay Code's immutable HarnessProfile.
No upstream prompt body or template is vendored or translated.

records.behaviorContract: Resolve one immutable catalog-specific schema snapshot and keep policy variants aligned with dispatcher and executor validation.
nonCopiedConstraints: Catalog identity and schema validation are Corelay Code-specific Go contracts.
No external tool schema catalog or generated binding is included.

records.behaviorContract: Convert canonical requests and streamed responses through protocol adapters while preserving role and tool-call ordering.
nonCopiedConstraints: The canonical state model is independently defined in Go for Corelay Code.
Golden fixtures are minimal newly authored interoperability examples.

records.behaviorContract: Expose Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Chat Completions, and OpenAI Responses ingress through one bounded canonical provider execution path.
nonCopiedConstraints: HTTP routing and canonical mapping are independent Corelay Code implementations.
No external server implementation or generated protocol handler is embedded.

records.behaviorContract: Select provider implementations behind one streaming Provider contract and bind the selected runtime target to server execution.
nonCopiedConstraints: The Provider interface predates this absorption work and remains Corelay Code-owned.
No external provider registry implementation is included.

records.behaviorContract: Compose provider metadata and eligible exact-target empirical evidence into one immutable run profile with explicit precedence.
nonCopiedConstraints: Capability evidence and precedence are Corelay Code-specific contracts.
No upstream model-name capability table is copied or embedded.

records.behaviorContract: Budget every completed request surface against model input, output, protocol, and safety reservations before provider execution.
nonCopiedConstraints: The estimator request surface and reduction records are Corelay Code-specific.
Boundary fixtures are newly authored deterministic token estimates.

records.behaviorContract: Trigger compaction from the resolved model window and converge provider failure or deadline to a deterministic bounded fallback.
nonCopiedConstraints: Compaction selection and fallback snapshots are independently designed for Corelay Code.
No upstream summarization prompt or compaction implementation is copied.

records.behaviorContract: Preserve objective, accepted plan, recent and orphan tool pairs, edits, and verification state in a bounded structured compaction snapshot.
nonCopiedConstraints: The snapshot schema and deterministic renderer are Corelay Code-specific.
No external conversation snapshot format or test fixture is included.

records.behaviorContract: Route an immutable catalog by deterministic local intent classification, fall back safely, and widen only after real execution.
nonCopiedConstraints: The category classifier and widening state are independent Corelay Code implementations.
No external router weights, model, or source code is embedded.

records.behaviorContract: Select a strict two-stage category router automatically when effective usable input is at most 16K, while allowing exact-target empirical evidence to override the fallback deterministically.
nonCopiedConstraints: The selector schema and state transition are independently designed for Corelay Code.
No upstream category prompt or routing implementation is copied.

records.behaviorContract: Bind patch-first, exact, whole-file, and corelay-waterfall policies to matching schemas and execution behavior.
nonCopiedConstraints: The unified-patch parser and edit policy mapping are independent Go implementations.
No external patch library or upstream edit source is vendored.

records.behaviorContract: Return deterministic fuzzy replacement outcomes and bounded candidate hints when exact edit matching fails.
nonCopiedConstraints: Fuzzy matching is an existing Corelay Code strength retained independently.
No external fuzzy matcher implementation or corpus is included.

records.behaviorContract: Run syntax or lint validation after edits and restore the original file on validation failure without bypassing sandbox policy.
nonCopiedConstraints: Rollback and lint selection are existing Corelay Code behavior.
No external lint executor or rollback implementation is copied.

records.behaviorContract: Connect a run-owned MCP generation before the first immutable catalog snapshot and bind calls to that exact generation.
nonCopiedConstraints: The MCP runtime ownership and generation binding are independently implemented for Corelay Code.
No external MCP client implementation or fixture server is vendored.

records.behaviorContract: Discover executable plugins before catalog snapshot and require identity-bound one-shot approval plus required sandbox isolation for every execution.
nonCopiedConstraints: Plugin manifests, bindings, and approval proofs are Corelay Code-specific.
No external plugin host, executable, or manifest fixture is included.

records.behaviorContract: Register one active run lifetime by session, propagate parent and explicit cancellation, release deterministically, and drain bounded shutdown.
nonCopiedConstraints: The run registry and adapter cancellation mapping are Corelay Code-specific.
No external cancellation registry or scheduler code is included.

records.behaviorContract: Measure protocol, context, routing, edit, repetition, and safety capabilities through deterministic isolated probes bound to an exact provider target.
nonCopiedConstraints: The profiler schema, scoring, and isolated executor are independently designed for Corelay Code.
No upstream probe implementation, benchmark corpus, or claimed score is copied.

records.behaviorContract: Keep calibration separate from holdout evidence and prevent automatic selection of low-confidence, failed, stale, corrupt, drifted, or manual-only profiles.
nonCopiedConstraints: Quarantine reasons and selection rules are Corelay Code-specific.
No external capability table, holdout corpus, or selection code is embedded.

records.behaviorContract: Linearize every run exit through one idempotent finalizer that pairs SessionStart and SessionEnd exactly once when started, terminalizes the recorder once, emits one typed done frame, and closes the stream.
nonCopiedConstraints: Lifecycle composition uses Corelay Code's existing hook registry and run context.
No external hook runner or lifecycle implementation is copied.

records.behaviorContract: Keep all 45 matrix rows synchronized with pinned behavior sources, independent implementation and test paths, non-copy constraints, repository-contained path validation, and a capability-by-capability independent semantic review while disclosing limits created by prior access.
nonCopiedConstraints: The ledger contains metadata and behavior contracts only, never upstream source bodies.
The audit reads repository-owned files and performs no network fetch or source generation.
